purpose: Nitroglycerin is used to treat and prevent chest pain called angina, which happens when your heart is not getting enough blood and oxygen. It works quickly to relieve chest pain during an episode, and certain forms can be used regularly to help prevent chest pain from happening. It is also sometimes used in heart failure and high blood pressure emergencies.
how_it_works: Nitroglycerin relaxes and widens the blood vessels in your body, including those around your heart. When your blood vessels are wider, blood flows more easily and your heart does not have to work as hard. This brings more oxygen to your heart and quickly relieves that tight, squeezing chest pain.
common_side_effects: Headache is very common, especially when you first start using it — this usually gets better over time. You may also feel dizzy or lightheaded, flushed or warm in your face, or notice a fast heartbeat. Your blood pressure may drop, so stand up slowly to avoid feeling faint.
warnings: Do not take nitroglycerin if you have recently taken erectile dysfunction medicines like sildenafil (Viagra), tadalafil (Cialis), or vardenafil (Levitra) — this combination can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure. Store your tablets in the original glass bottle away from heat, light, and moisture. If chest pain does not improve after one tablet under your tongue in 5 minutes, call 911 immediately — do not wait. Do not stop using this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor.
typical_dosing: For sudden chest pain, place one small tablet under your tongue and let it dissolve — do not swallow it. If pain continues after 5 minutes, you may take a second tablet. After another 5 minutes you may take a third if needed. If pain is not gone after 3 tablets (15 minutes total), call 911 right away. Patches, ointments, and long-acting tablets are used on a regular schedule your doctor will set for prevention — follow your doctor's instructions carefully.
